references.text: Addresses the corresponding principle that the priest shall assess what a person can afford if they are too poor to bring the prescribed offering.
Shows the same principle of adjusting offerings based on financial ability for those who are poor.
Describes a similar provision where the priest evaluates what a poor woman can afford as an offering after childbirth.
Contains provisions for the poor who cannot afford regular offerings when being cleansed from leprosy, with the priest assessing their ability.
The context of vows concerning persons to the Lord and the various valuations underlying them before the exception for the poor in verse 8.
Mary and Joseph brought an offering for the poor (two turtledoves) according to the provisions in the Law of Moses regarding adjustment based on financial ability.
Paul emphasizes that generosity is judged by what one has, not by what one does not have, reflecting the principle of giving according to one's means.
